[HSS] Add IncludeRegisterRequest/Response to iFC ApplicationServer

Read include_register_request and include_register_response (bool)
from each iFC's application_server and emit them inside <Extension>
of <ApplicationServer> in the Cx User-Data (TS 29.228 Table E.2).

Both default to false, so existing profiles are unchanged.
WebUI does not edit ifc; the keys must be set in MongoDB directly.

Issues: #4898

[5GC] Handle SBI resource exhaustion across network functions

Handle context and session pool exhaustion gracefully instead of
returning misleading HTTP errors or terminating on assertions.

- UDM: Return 500 INSUFFICIENT_RESOURCES when UE or session
  context allocation fails, while preserving existing 404 handling
  for invalid or missing contexts.
- AUSF: Distinguish UE allocation failure from missing
  authentication contexts.
- PCF: Handle AM, SM, and application session allocation failures
  without assertions, and clean up partially created contexts.
- BSF: Return an appropriate server error when the session pool
  is exhausted, preserving validation errors for invalid addresses.
- NRF: Replace incorrect resource exhaustion responses with
  500 INSUFFICIENT_RESOURCES.
- SEPP: Handle peer node allocation failure without terminating
  the process.

Preserve existing request validation and normal error responses
while reporting resource exhaustion consistently.

Issues: #4939

core: ogs_tlv_add(): Skip 0-length memcpy

memcpy with NULL arg and length=0 is undefined behavior on older C specs
and results in a no-op on newer ones, so no need to call it.
Morever, it makes no sense to assign new->value = head->buff_ptr in that
case because the pointer passed to ogs_tlv_add(value) may be undefined
(eg. NULL, some random memory, etc.); better keep it to NULL in that
case.

Related PR #4953

[AMF] Resolve pending 5G-GUTIs on registration retry

A UE can reconnect with the 5G-GUTI received in Registration Accept
before sending Registration Complete. The AMF previously failed to
resolve that GUTI and sent an Identity Request.

Index the pending GUTI after successfully sending Registration Accept
and expose it to NAS Registration Request lookup. Validate the stored
NAS security context, ngKSI, and message integrity before associating
a new NG connection. Remove the pending entry on deregistration or
UE removal.

Add regression coverage for a reconnect before Registration Complete,
including an invalid MAC followed by a valid retry at the same COUNT.

Issues #4949

[MME] Resolve pending EPS GUTIs on attach retry

A UE can retry Attach with the EPS GUTI from Attach Accept before
the MME receives Attach Complete. Make that GUTI available to NAS
Attach Request lookup after a successful send or T3450 retransmission.

Validate eKSI and NAS integrity before associating the new S1
connection with the existing UE context. Clear the pending lookup
entry when the attach is aborted, the UE deregisters, or the context
is removed.

Extend the Attach GUTI test to check that an invalid MAC releases
only the new S1 connection and that a valid retry at the same COUNT
receives Authentication Request.

Issues: #4949

[SBI] Run graceful shutdown on the NF worker thread

The termination thread can send NRF deregistration and HTTP/2 GOAWAY
while the NF worker is still using the same libcurl handles and pollset.
Concurrent access can abort the process during shutdown.

Run shutdown signaling on the worker and keep polling during the
300 ms grace period. Join the worker before tearing down SBI resources.
In AMF, close the NGAP listeners and gNB connections before the grace
period to prevent repeated EOF reads on the shared pollset.

Treat a failed NRF deregistration send as nonfatal. Suppress queue
errors for OGS_DONE while still freeing rejected events and their
buffers, including the AMF delayed-send packet. Update the NF FSM
guard comments to reflect the new shutdown order.

Issues #4969

[SMF] Release rejected sessions on N1N2 transfer timeout

When the AMF does not respond to an N1N2MessageTransfer carrying a
PDU Session Establishment Reject, the SBI client wait timer removes
the transaction but leaves the local session allocated. This retains
session resources and keeps pfcp_sessions_active from decreasing.

Clear the local session when the timed-out transaction targets
namf-comm and the session is in smf_gsm_state_5gc_n1_n2_reject,
matching the cleanup performed when an AMF response arrives.

Leave PCF/UDM cleanup timeouts and other session states unchanged.

Issues #4878

[SMF] Fix QoS flow description encoding on N16

TS 29.502 requires qosFlowDescription to carry the full QoS flow
descriptions IE, including the IEI and two-octet length. Encode the
full IE in H-SMF session setup and update messages.

Validate the IEI and length on the V-SMF before passing the value to
the NAS encoder. Reject malformed descriptions in update requests
before replacing the session's QoS flow lists. Keep qosRules encoded
from octet 4 as specified.

Issues #4974
Update CLA

[MME] Reject Path Switch Requests for inactive S1 contexts

Releasing the active S1 connection during an S1 handover can leave the
prepared target context pointing to the MME UE. A subsequent X2 Path
Switch Request can resolve that context even though the MME UE no longer
has an active S1 connection. The lookup in sgw_ue_check_if_relocated()
then returns NULL and triggers an assertion.

Verify that the resolved S1 context is still the MME UE's active context
before updating UE state. Send Path Switch Request Failure and return
if the MME UE is missing or the context is inactive.

Issues: #4992

[DBI] Ignore array entries beyond the maximum (#4991)

A subscriber document with more array entries than the fixed limit
(MSISDN, Slice, Session, PCC Rule, Flow, IFC, SPT) aborted
HSS/UDR/PCF/PCRF on ogs_assert() in lib/dbi. Keep the entries up to
the maximum and log an error instead.

The WebUI still accepts more entries than the limit.

[SBI] Validate SUPI inputs across NFs

Malformed SUPIs in SM Policy Create could reach assertions in PCF
policy lookup.

Add ogs_supi_is_valid() in lib/proto using the existing identity parser
and IMSI validator. Reuse it in ogs_supi_to_imsi_bcd() to centralize
validation without additional parsing.

Validate SUPIs before context lookup, creation or update in AMF,
AUSF, UDM, UDR, PCF, BSF and SMF. Distinguish SUCI inputs and validate
optional SUPIs only when present.

Issues #4994

[PCF] Remove NBSF discovery xact before sending the response

When NBSF discovery finds no BSF, the PCF sends the SM Policy
Association create response and only then removes the xact. Sending
the response closes the HTTP/2 stream, and closing the stream already
removes the xact attached to it. The second ogs_sbi_xact_remove() then
frees discovery_option again (heap-use-after-free).

Remove the xact first, as the other SBI response handlers already do.

Issues: #4955

ausf: handle outbound SBI failures without aborting

Return failure from authentication, confirmation and deletion handlers
when discovery or send fails. The wrapper already sends an error response,
and the existing UE exception path removes the authentication context
instead of asserting on resource exhaustion.

Issues: #4472 and #4473

Revert "sbi: cancel pending outbound xacts on stream close"

This reverts commit 68ab28cd86bba6f83ec36d2a1f491ea3db5251b0.

Closing an inbound HTTP stream does not mean that the associated NF
procedure can be abandoned. Automatic transaction cancellation can
interrupt SMF session teardown and free transactions while response
handlers still use them, as in #4995.

Leave transaction cleanup to NF response/timeout handling and SBI
object removal. Preserve subsequent independent fixes.

Related: #4472, #4473, #4995

ausf/udm: validate 5G-AKA hex fields before use

ausf_nausf_auth_handle_authenticate_confirmation() decoded
ConfirmationData.resStar with ogs_ascii_to_hex() into an uninitialized
stack buffer and ignored how many bytes were written. A short or empty
resStar from the serving network left the remainder of res_star
uninitialized, and that is what memcmp() then compared against
XRES* to decide the authentication result.

udm_nudm_ueau_handle_get() had the same pattern for the RAND and AUTS
of ResynchronizationInfo, so the RAND check and the MAC-S check read
uninitialized bytes when either string was short.

Decode these fields with ogs_hex_from_string_checked() and reject the
request with 400 when a value is not exactly the expected number of
hex digits. Apply the same check to RAND, XRES* and KAUSF from the
UDM in ausf_nudm_ueau_handle_get(), decoding into temporaries before
updating the UE context, as the AMF already does for the AUSF vector.

gtp/nas: bound IPv6 prefix length in packet filter components

ogs_gtp2_parse_tft() and ogs_nas_parse_qos_rules() copied the one-octet
prefix length of an IPv6 address/prefix length packet filter component
without checking it, so a UE could supply any value up to 255. The SMF
hands that value to n2mask(), which writes ceil(n/8) bytes starting at
the 16-byte mask array of ogs_ipfw_rule_t, so a prefix length above 128
writes past the mask into the neighbouring fields of the rule.

Reject a prefix length above 128 in both parsers, matching the check the
ipfw string parser already performs before it calls n2mask().

Signed-off-by: Soma Aishwarya <soma@digiscrypt.com>

mme: bound SGsAP DOWNLINK-UNITDATA NAS message container length

The SGsAP NAS message container length is one octet, but the EPS NAS
message container buffer holds OGS_NAS_MAX_MESSAGE_CONTAINER_LEN (250)
octets. A 251..255 octet container from the VLR was copied past the
buffer by emm_build_downlink_nas_transport(), and the encoder then read
past its stack copy, sending those bytes to the UE.

Reject the oversized container in the SGsAP handler before UE lookup,
and refuse it in the builder as well.

[AMF] Handle Handover Request build and send failures

If the NGAP Handover Request cannot be encoded or sent, release the
temporary target RAN UE context and send Handover Preparation Failure
to the source gNB.

Remove the assertion in the SMF response handler so the AMF can clear
the stored N2 transfers even if sending the failure response also fails.

Related to #4909

smf: Bound UE-requested QoS bit rates

Decode NAS bit rates using checked 64-bit arithmetic to prevent
integer overflow. Cap UE-requested GFBR and MFBR at the NGAP limit
before updating the QoS flow so oversized values cannot trigger
an assertion when SMF builds the N2 transfer.

mme: reject a truncated Service Request before decoding

[SMF] Ignore duplicate QFI in PDU Session Resource Modify Response

Skip QoS flows already present in qos_flow_to_modify_list to avoid
inserting the same node twice and creating a circular list.

Based on PR #4913 by linouxis9.

s1ap: reject unsupported eNB IDs without aborting

Return an error for unsupported or malformed eNB IDs and handle it
in all MME callers, including S1 Setup, Configuration Transfer,
Handover Required and Gn RAN Information Relay.

smf: bound ePCO size before encoding

mme: ignore an Identity Response when the IMSI is already known

mme: keep a second PDN request out of the attach path

Drop standalone PDN Connectivity Requests during Attach before session

Validate the Attach Complete ESM container in its handler. Discard queued
ESM messages for removed UEs or disallowed EMM states, and document ESM

Related PR #4920

amf, ausf, upf: test identity indexes when another context takes a key

These are the identity indexes GHSA-7g3v-g4gp-p624 names, where a
second context takes over a key that the first one still holds: the AMF
SUPI index when a SUPI is re-assigned, the AUSF SUPI and SUCI indexes
when a UE authenticates again before its old context is removed, and
the UPF UE address index when a session of the same PFCP node takes
over an address. Each of these entries kept the first context's key,
which was then freed with that context, until d6e4125e5 ("core: make
hash tables own their keys") made the tables keep their own copy.

Each test checks the contents and length of the key the index holds,
then lets the first context change, free or reuse its key, and checks
that the second context is still found and the indexed key unchanged.

Add ausf-unit and upf-unit test executables for the AUSF and UPF tests,
which link their NF library apart from the unit executable.
docs: troubleshoot: explain martian drop when UE and UPF share a host

sepp: only relay N32-f requests to home PLMN NFs

request_handler() relays a peer SEPP's request to whatever
3gpp-Sbi-Target-apiRoot names whenever ogs_sbi_fqdn_in_vplmn() does
not classify it as a foreign PLMN. IP literals and arbitrary host names
fall into that branch, so a peer could make the SEPP send requests to
any host:port it can reach and get the response back.

Check the host returned by ogs_sbi_getaddr_from_uri(), which is the one
that gets dialed, and only relay when it is a
<...>.mncXXX.mccXXX.3gppnetwork.org FQDN of a serving PLMN.
amf/mme: set T3522, T3570, T3422, T3460 and T3470 to 6 seconds
amf/mme: reject a registration or attach with no encryption algorithm
amf/mme: discard a NAS message that fails its checks
amf/mme: keep a failed MAC from invalidating the security context
amf/mme: protect a retransmitted NAS message under the next NAS COUNT
amf/mme: send Criticality Diagnostics for missing IEs and logical errors
open5gs-dbctl: Support inserting IMEIs into eir db
amf/mme: discard a Security Mode Complete that is not ciphered
mme: ignore an ESM Information Response with no pending request

amf/mme: keep a registered context until the identity is authenticated

An Identity Response that names the SUCI (IMSI) of a registered UE moved
that UE's context and sessions into the context of the new connection
before any authentication. When the authentication failed, the UE was
left with no context and its sessions were released. A Registration
(Attach) Request that names the UE on the connection waiting for the
Identity Response did the same.

TS 24.501 5.5.1.2.8 f) and TS 24.301 5.5.1.2.7 f) delete the existing
context only once the request turns out to come from the genuine UE.
amf_ue_set_suci() and mme_ue_set_imsi() now leave the existing context
and its index entry as they are. The AMF releases it into the new
context when the AUSF confirms the SUPI (amf_ue_set_supi(), as for a
re-registration with a fresh SUCI) and releases the moved sessions after
the authentication; the MME releases it when the Authentication Response
passes.

Signed-off-by: valentin <valentin@devling.xyz>

nas: bound S-NSSAI length in ogs_nas_parse_nssai

ogs_nas_parse_s_nssai() trusts the S-NSSAI length octet, and
ogs_nas_parse_nssai() never checked it against the bytes left in the
NSSAI IE, so a truncated S-NSSAI was completed from the zeroed tail of
the buffer. An S-NSSAI with an invalid length did not advance the
position either, so the same bytes were re-parsed until
OGS_MAX_NUM_OF_SLICE empty entries had been counted.

Reject an S-NSSAI that runs past the IE and stop at the first one that
fails to parse.

crypt: remove unused KASUMI implementation

KASUMI was built into libogscrypt but had no callers. EPS and 5GS
NAS security do not use it.

core: remove Orcania code from ogs-strings

Replace ogs_msprintf_debug() and ogs_mstrcatf_debug() with a shared
formatter adapted from musl v1.2.5. Retain the MIT notice and free
the temporary buffer if the second vsnprintf() call fails.

Format uint64_t values directly as unpadded hexadecimal, preserving
the empty string for zero. Remove the four unused trim helpers and
the Orcania notices.

Suppress expected invalid-SUPI errors in supi_validation(). Restore
the original core log level after each case and retain diagnostics
at debug and trace levels.

crypt: replace GnuTLS-derived PEM parser and test vectors

Require an exact BEGIN label so a block with a longer label sharing
the same prefix is skipped. Continue accepting mismatched END labels
and whitespace in the body. Reject embedded NUL bytes and malformed
Base64, and report missing boundaries without logging PEM contents.

Replace the GnuTLS-derived test vectors with Open5GS fixtures covering
label matching, whitespace, double padding, and malformed inputs.
Suppress expected parser errors during negative tests and restore
the previous log level after each case.

crypt: reimplement SNOW 3G integrity on the existing core

Implement UIA2 using the existing SNOW 3G keystream generator in
openssl/snow_core.c. Preserve the snow_3g_f9() interface and remove
the unused reference cipher and keystream entry points.

Construct FRESH with an unsigned BEARER shift to avoid undefined
behavior for bearer values from 16 to 31.

Add UIA2 and 128-EIA1 known-answer vectors, including checks that
unused bits in the final byte do not affect the MAC.

crypt: replace the ZUC reference code with GmSSL ZUC-128

Adapt the ZUC-128 core and EIA3 sliding-window MAC from GmSSL
commit 24ae482701a7b124826c382fffc55c19f76d475d. Preserve the EEA3
and EIA3 interfaces, including in-place encryption and the
host-order MAC.

Use per-call state and generate the keystream without a
message-sized allocation. Remove the unused stateful keystream
API and document the upstream source and Open5GS changes.

Extend the TS 35.223 tests to cover non-byte-aligned inputs,
unused bits, and in-place encryption.

tests: preserve UPF unit test log levels after context initialization

Restore the saved PFCP and UPF log levels immediately after context
initialization, which resets them to the core default level.

nas: bound the length of every LV/TLV IE encoder

The generated LV and TLV encoders in lib/nas/eps and lib/nas/5gs copy
the IE into a local of the IE type and then write length + 1 (or
length + 2) octets from it, trusting the length field. The decoders
already refuse an IE longer than its type; the encoders did not, so a
length set beyond the buffer by the caller made them read past the
local and put those stack octets into the message.

One caller that can do this is the MME's SGsAP DOWNLINK-UNITDATA path,
where the VLR's NAS message container may be up to 255 octets against
the 250-octet buffer of ogs_nas_eps_message_container_t; #4882 added the
check at that handler. This change closes the encoding step itself for
every IE, so no other caller can make an encoder copy more than the
IE holds.

- nas-message.py (EPS and 5GS): every LV/TLV encoder returns -1 when
  the length does not fit its type, as its decoder does (66 EPS and 85
  5GS encoders); ies.c regenerated from the existing caches, with no
  other change.

Add a test to the NAS message unit tests that encodes an EPS message
container at the maximum length and checks that one octet more is
refused.

[AMF] Ignore a late UDM purge after re-registration

A UE that deregisters and immediately registers again can leave the
deregistration's Nudm_UECM PATCH (purgeFlag) outstanding while the new
registration moves to security-mode or initial-context-setup. Neither
state expects that response, so it reaches ogs_assert_if_reached() and
the AMF aborts.

Ignore it in both states, as gmm_state_authentication already does
(#4074).

[AMF] Ignore failed late UECM purge responses during registration

Move the UECM response status check into the PUT branch in
gmm_state_initial_context_setup().

This allows late deregistration PATCH responses to reach the ignore
branch even on failure, preventing them from rejecting a subsequent
registration.

Follow-up to PR #4957.

crypt: remove unused SHA-1 and HMAC-SHA1

Nothing outside the tests uses them. Drop the test cases as well.

Also fix the license header of ogs-strings.[ch] to AGPL, and
shorten the aws-c-io note in ogs_fbase64_decode().

docs: update third-party copyright and license notices

Document licenses and attribution for third-party code, libraries,
and WebUI assets.

Record musl, aws-c-io, SNOW 3G, and GmSSL provenance, and update
debian/copyright to reflect the current source layout.

[HSS] Restore MSISDN identities on Cx re-registration

After an HSS restart, the S-CSCF can still have the subscriber profile.
When SAR indicates USER_DATA_ALREADY_AVAILABLE, the HSS skips profile
generation and leaves the MSISDN-derived SIP and TEL identities missing.
Subsequent LIRs for those identities cannot find the assigned S-CSCF.

Associate the MSISDN identities during Cx registration and
re-registration regardless of profile availability. Generate the
profile XML only when the S-CSCF requests it.

Related PR: #4976

cosmetic: sepp: Enclose else branch in brackets

As usual C style, if the if branch has brackets, add brackets for the
else branch too. Otherwise it's specially confusing in this path due to
the comment block below.

sepp: Fix assert hit on exchange-capability received before registration to NRF

1- open5gs-seppd starts and attempts to register with NRF but fails. Hence,
since no answer is received it never initializes the handshake fsm
(sepp_node->sm).
2- Then, it receives a POST /n32c-handshake/v1/exchange-capability (supportedCap=TLS) from
a peer SEPP. If the SEPP was configured in the config file
(sepp_node_add(receiver) in context.c), the code path would find and
set sepp_node pointer, but it's sepp_node->sm FSM was never yet
initialized.
3- "ogs_assert(OGS_FSM_STATE(&sepp_node->sm));" further below hits and
open5gs-seppd crashes.

Fix it by making sure to call sepp_handshake_fsm_init() if the sepp_node
is found and its fsm was not yet set up.

Take the chance to do early break in the POST exchange-capability path
to simplify the indenation.

sepp: Make sure to enable handhsake-sm establishment when obtaining SEPP Peer List

If a peer sepp was intiially learned/added through received N32C POST
exchange-capability, then its handshake-sm is created re-establishment disabled.

If later on the peer sends exchange-capability secCap=NONE to terminate
the session, and internally the sepp_node goes to "terminated" state,
the handshake-sm is left created and with re-establishmed disabled
(t_establish_interval).

If then later on the sepp registers through NRF and re-learns about that
same peer seep, since the handshake-sm is already created it will not
attempt re-establishment despite it being terminated beforehand because
the "!OGS_FSM_STATE(&sepp_node->sm)" won't hit and hence
sepp_handshake_fsm_init(try_to_establish=true) is not called.

Fix the later code path scenario by making sure to enable
re-establishment timer if the FSM is in terminated or exception state.

[SEPP] Fix N32-c establishment around NRF registration

Start the establishment timer after NRF registration when an inbound
request left a configured peer in will_establish without a running
timer. Skip peers without an outbound N32-c client.

Return HTTP 503 if an inbound request would negotiate TLS before the
local serving PLMN list is available. This lets the peer retry instead
of establishing with an empty PLMN list. Log the sender when deferring
and preserve existing handling of NONE and unsupported capabilities.

Follow-up to #4984 and #4985.

[HSS] Derive SIP IMPU domain from the IMPI realm

The HSS uses the Visited-Network-Identifier from UAR as the domain
of SIP IMPUs generated from MSISDNs. When this identifier differs
from the subscriber's home domain, LIR lookups for the home-domain
SIP URI can fail.

Use the IMPI realm when associating MSISDNs during registration and
re-registration. Fall back to the Visited-Network-Identifier if the
realm is missing or empty.

Related PR: #4989

[SMF] Send subsSessAmbr even without DN-Authorization

subsSessAmbr was only sent to the PCF (and authSessAmbr only returned)
when DN-Authorization was negotiated. That feature is for DN-AAA data.
The subscribed Session-AMBR from UDM should always be sent, except for
emergency sessions (TS 29.512 4.2.2.2, 4.2.2.5).

+#### UE Gets an IP Address but Cannot Reach the Internet
+If the UE registers and the PDU session is established (e.g. UERANSIM prints `PDU Session establishment is successful` and creates `uesimtun0`), but the UE cannot reach the Internet, first check that [IP forwarding and the NAT rule]({{ site.url }}{{ site.baseurl }}/docs/guide/01-quickstart#UEInternet) are configured on the UPF host.
+
+__UE simulator and UPF running on the same host:__
+If UERANSIM (or another UE simulator) runs on the same host as the UPF, the UE IP address (e.g. `10.45.0.2`) is assigned to `uesimtun0` on that host. When the UPF writes the decapsulated uplink packet to `ogstun`, the Linux kernel sees a packet whose source address belongs to the host itself and drops it as a *martian* packet. Uplink packets are visible on `ogstun`, but never leave the WAN interface.
+
+You can confirm this by enabling martian logging:
+```bash
+$ sudo sysctl -w net.ipv4.conf.all.log_martians=1
+$ sudo dmesg | grep martian
+IPv4: martian source 8.8.8.8 from 10.45.0.2, on dev ogstun
+```
+
+To avoid this, run the gNB/UE simulator on a separate machine/VM, or in a separate network namespace connected to the host with a veth pair:
+```bash
+$ sudo ip netns add ran
+$ sudo ip link add veth-core type veth peer name veth-ran
+$ sudo ip link set veth-ran netns ran
+$ sudo ip addr add 10.10.0.1/24 dev veth-core
+$ sudo ip link set veth-core up
+$ sudo ip netns exec ran ip addr add 10.10.0.2/24 dev veth-ran
+$ sudo ip netns exec ran ip link set veth-ran up
+$ sudo ip netns exec ran ip link set lo up
+```
+
+Bind the AMF NGAP server and the UPF GTP-U server to the host side of the veth pair, then restart `open5gs-amfd` and `open5gs-upfd`.
+
+```diff
+$ diff -u /etc/open5gs/amf.yaml.old /etc/open5gs/amf.yaml
+   ngap:
+     server:
+-      - address: 127.0.0.5
++      - address: 10.10.0.1
+
+$ diff -u /etc/open5gs/upf.yaml.old /etc/open5gs/upf.yaml
+   gtpu:
+     server:
+-      - address: 127.0.0.7
++      - address: 10.10.0.1
+```
+
+In the UERANSIM gNB configuration, set `ngapIp` and `gtpIp` to `10.10.0.2` and the AMF address to `10.10.0.1`. Then run the gNB, UE and test traffic inside the namespace:
+```bash
+$ sudo ip netns exec ran ./build/nr-gnb -c config/open5gs-gnb.yaml
+$ sudo ip netns exec ran ./build/nr-ue -c config/open5gs-ue.yaml
+$ sudo ip netns exec ran ping -I uesimtun0 8.8.8.8
+```
